newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Police officer killed in Dominican Republic strike.
newsitem.headline: Police officer killed in Dominican Republic strike.

text.p: A police officer was shot dead and at least three people were wounded in the Dominican Republic when a 24-hour strike turned violent on Tuesday, police said.

The casualties occurred during a confrontation between police and demonstrators early in the morning in the southern city of Barahona. One of the injured was a 12-year-old child who suffered a gunshot wound in the melee, police said.
National police chief Major General Miguel Sanz Jiminian called the confrontation a "terrorist action" and said that about 20 people had been arrested.
Workers also demonstrated in Azua, another southern city.
The strike was called to demand that President Leonel Fernandez's government initiate public works projects which would generate jobs.

Fernandez was inaugurated last August to succeed Joaquin Balaguer as president. Balaguer's decades in office were marked by a steady run of massive public works projects which drained the nation's economy but provided thousands of jobs.
The government offered no immediate official response to the strikers' demands.
